red_flags.detail: q3_lemmas.py (the Q3 L2/L3 lemma verification: sector-sum decomposition and the 300/300 uniform jump law), q2_mechanism.py (the Q2 SU(3)_2/E6-k=2 character-blindness mechanism), and n2_su3_13_measure.py (the flagship SU(3)_13 prediction-first hit, clock=12) all print their results to stdout only, with no JSON/data dump. Their execution transcripts (q3_lemmas.log, q2_mechanism.log, n2_su3_13.log) are hashed in ORIGINALS_MANIFEST.txt as received but match the repo-wide *.log gitignore rule and are confirmed absent from the checked-out arc directory (`find ... -name '*.log' -o -name '*.out'` returns nothing). The claimed numeric outputs of these three scripts are therefore not independently checkable against any committed artifact -- only against the prose recap in FINDINGS_CC2.md/ADDENDUM_N2.md/PROOF_SKETCH.md.

N2's amended (stage-split) clock law was constructed after observing which 7 of 19 rungs the verbatim H-R2 rule missed (12/19), i.e. the k=1/k=2 anomaly clauses are a post-hoc pattern extraction from the failure set, then declared to score 15/15 on the remainder. This is disclosed candidly ('CORRECTION LOGGED', the addendum is explicitly sealed before the one true test) rather than hidden, and the one genuine out-of-sample test (SU(3)_13) hit prediction-first -- but the law-fitting-to-failures structure itself is a standard overfitting risk that a single confirmed rung does not fully retire.

Nearly every number-theoretic 'law' in this arc (clock law, splitting law, generic-rung law, jump law) is validated only against the same closed object (the E6 Z-ladder / A_n level algebras built from a single golden matrix A1) via the object's own committed engine scripts. There is no external dataset or independent physical system against which these laws are checked; internal cross-pipeline agreement (e.g. Jeffrey vs B600 engine) is the closest thing to independence achieved, and this is disclosed as such ('the heavy enumerations rest on the sending seat's sealed two-pipeline identity').

level7_run.py's own docstring is a stale copy-paste header ('Level-5 (kappa=17) run') from an earlier level's template script, though the code correctly builds Level(7) matching PREREG_L7.md's kappa=19 and the committed readouts. Not a computational error, but a documentation-hygiene defect that could mislead a future reader auditing this exact file.

The arc's absence-sweep on B480 and B544 shows those two ARCS' original headline claims (level-ratio <r>=0.16 at N=181,301; Sturmian 610/610; itinerary 99.95%) rest on no committed reproducer anywhere in the repo, and this arc's own from-scratch reimplementations either fail a basic consistency check (B480's quantization is not a faithful SL(2,Z/N) representation) or land 4-5 orders of magnitude off the claimed constant (B544's Omega* differs from the quoted figure from the 6th significant digit). This is a finding ABOUT other arcs (B480, B544), surfaced honestly here rather than about B646 itself, but it means those two original claims stand un-reproduced as of this integration.
